note: Modules implemented in BOTH TypeScript and Python. Each must be covered by a contract corpus. ADR-0009 trigger line: more than 3 duplicated modules, or a second 'the two sides disagreed' incident, means evaluate a single Rust/WASM kernel.

limit_history.reason: The line (3) was crossed by E2/E3 work: ids, structure-validity and the edit algebra were added on both sides (6 modules). Evaluated per ADR-0009 section 'Trigger evaluation 2026-10-06'; decision: keep two implementations, new line 6.

O-01 needs the kinematic objectives on the Python side to use mature optimisers; they are a leaf function over the already-duplicated gait metrics, checked on a 123-case corpus generated by the TS reference (one documented deviation in a corner case, EXPERIMENTS 16). Evaluated again against ADR-0009: same conclusion, line now 7. Three limits raised in one session is a pattern: the next duplicated module should go to the user as a decision about a single kernel, not to another edit of this number.

Browser simulation (MuJoCo WebAssembly) needs the MJCF builder in TypeScript. As ADR-0009 asked for the 8th module, this went to the user as a decision about a single kernel: they chose to accept the 8th duplicate (Pyodide / Rust kernels not evaluated). The corpus is the strictest kind: byte-identical MJCF text for 34 cases (every shared scene, other linkages, every terrain kind, solver/drive/walker options), generated by the Python builder; mutation-checked (a 1e-7 relative change or a swapped RNG draw fails it).
